findings.title: deleteMany OR branch deletes reminders of any method
findings.body: The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter, so this SMS cron will delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP workflow reminders too as soon as any other job/code path increments their retryCount past 1. Since the column is shared across all reminder methods, this risks silently destroying pending email/WhatsApp reminders. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch.

findings.title: Prisma update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` added at the start of the catch block is awaited outside of any try/catch. If the record was deleted concurrently (P2025) or the DB call fails, the rejection propagates out of the loop, the remaining unscheduled reminders are never processed and the endpoint returns a 500 with no response body written. Wrap this update in its own try/catch (and do it after logging).

findings.title: Use atomic increment instead of read-modify-write for retryCount
findings.body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (common with slow Twilio calls), both write the same value and one failure is lost, so a reminder can retry indefinitely. Use `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`.

findings.title: No retry accounting when message or sendTo is missing
findings.body: If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is null, the reminder is skipped without incrementing retryCount and without marking it scheduled, so it will be re-fetched every cron run until its scheduledDate passes — the exact loop this PR intends to stop. Increment retryCount (or mark it unschedulable) in this branch too.
